name: University of Essex

settingEvidence.evidence: Set within 200 acres of award-winning parkland - Wivenhoe Park and located two miles from the historic city centre of Colchester

fees.text: £10,050 per year for new Home (UK) and Channel Islands students starting in 2027-28. A study abroad year costs 15% and a placement year 20% of the standard fee for that year, and fees increase for each academic year of study.

source.evidence: Following the UK Government's recent decision to increase fees for the academic year 2027-28, our tuition fee for new Home, UK and Channel Islands students is £10,050 per year.

livingCosts.text: On-campus single rooms and studios cost about £127.89 to £257.88 a week in 2026-27 (rent includes bills and Wi-Fi; undergraduate contracts are normally 39 weeks). Shared twin en suite rooms are £82.88 to £92.89 per person a week.

source.evidence: North Towers - single room with shared facilities - £127.89 per week...The Copse - self-contained studio - £257.88 per week

openDays.text: Next open day: Saturday 7 November 2026 at the Colchester Campus. No later dates are published yet.

source.evidence: Our next Open Day - 7 November 2026

contextual.summary: Essex may make UK-resident applicants who meet one of its listed criteria (for example free school meals, POLAR4 quintiles 1-2, care experience or young carer) a contextual offer of up to two A-level grades below the standard offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two A-level grades, or equivalent, below the standard conditional offer. Course pages show 120 instead of 128 tariff points for BSc Economics and 96 instead of 112 for BA Economics.

criteria.detail: Students residing in the UK who are estranged from their parents.
Young carer: students residing in the UK who helped to look after someone in their family who is ill, disabled, has a mental health condition.
Military families: students residing in the UK who have a parent or carer serving in the Armed Forces.
Where residing in the UK, students with 'refugee status' or 'Humanitarian Protection', and asylum seekers.
Students residing in the UK, who are (or have been) eligible or receiving free school meals during their secondary education.
Students residing in the UK where there is low progression to Higher Education, defined as Quintiles 1 and 2 from OfS POLAR4 data.
Students residing in the UK who have experience of care, for example foster care, residential care, being looked after at home under a supervision order, or kinship care (officially or informally).
Disability: students residing in the UK who have declared one or more disability type on their application.

contextual.rulesText: Applicants who apply in the 2027 cycle may be made a contextual offer based on one of the listed criteria. You do not need to do anything: apply as normal and, if you are eligible, your offer letter will tell you. Contextual offers are available for most but not all courses (not for degrees with a foundation year, among others). Not eligible: second/final year entrants, recognised transfer programme applicants, applicants taking vocational or work-based learning qualifications, and applicants taking qualifications graded pass or fail. Your offer may still include specific subject or GCSE conditions.

notes: Essex's course pages show an October 2027 start and no 2028-entry pages are published yet (checked 2026-10-21), so all courses use 2027 entry.

Essex states offers as UCAS tariff points from a minimum of the equivalent of 2 full A-levels (for example 128 points for BSc Economics), not as A-level grades. The only subject requirement listed is GCSE Mathematics (grade 4 or 5 depending on the course).
Essex is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and the course pages name no admissions test.

Courses recorded are from Essex's Economics subject area. Not recorded (course limit): BA and BSc Management Economics, BA Financial Economics, BA Social Sciences, BSc Actuarial Science, Integrated Master in Economics, BA International Affairs and Economics (final-year entry for transfer students) and BSc Economics (Including Foundation Year).

Essex says UK students from a household income of up to £35,000 may be eligible for its Essex Futures Bursary, a support package worth up to £3,000 (https://www.essex.ac.uk/life/cost-of-living-support).
Essex says it guarantees accommodation for the duration of your course (terms and conditions apply).
